content: ‘The NCP faction will remain steadfast in supporting AIFB’s alignment with the INDIA bloc and carry forward its fight against alleged discrepancies in the SIR of electoral rolls’

title: BJP faces crisis in Thiruvananthapuram Corporation as councillor R. Sreelekha mulls resignation
content: The former DGP mentions in her ward’s WhatsApp group that she had informed the Mayor through a letter on September 30 about resigning as a councillor for personal reasons. Mayor says the letter only contained her inconveniences and that a councillor has to submit resignation letter to Corporation Secretary. The latter denies receiving any such communication

title: Delhi Police personnel were removing identity badges before detaining protesters: CPI MP to Amit Shah
content: Citing Supreme Court directives and Delhi Police Standing Order No. 51, Rajya Sabha MP Sandosh Kumar says identification is essential for accountability when police use coercive powers against citizens

title: Sreelekha’s ‘resignation’ exposes BJP’s internal troubles in Keralam, says Govindan
content: CPI(M) State secretary says some people enter politics with expectations of personal benefits and may not remain in active politics for long

title: Work on organ transplant institute in Kozhikode to be completed in 30 months, says Satheesan
content: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan says that ₹271 crore is being set aside for the institute coming up on a 20-acre plot in Chevayur. All services related to organ transplantation will be brought under one roof to reduce the cost of surgery to one-third.

title: India Summons Top Pakistan Diplomat To Protest Cross-Border Infiltration
content: India has asked the Pakistani diplomat to ensure that his country respects the sanctity of the International Border, strictly observes relevant bilateral arrangements, and mandates its forces to exercise effective control to prevent unauthorised movement from its side.

title: 'God Made Me This Way': LGBTQ Influencer Mad Sandhu, Murdered In Amritsar, Had This To Say To 'Culture' Trolls
content: Mad Sandhu spoke publicly about his life for years before his death. "I ignored the negative comments and kept the positive ones in my mind... It doesn't matter now. I know how to live my life," he said in interviews.

title: Adani Airports To Redevelop North Section Of Mumbai Airport's Terminal 1B
content: The redevelopment will temporarily deoperationalise around 5 million passengers a year, or about 9 per cent of Mumbai airport's total annual traffic of nearly 55 million passengers, the company said.

content: Frank Strada, commissioner of the Department of Correction, will step down this month, Governor Bill Lee said.

content: A clean India meant a healthy India, and a healthy India meant a stronger, more productive and more prosperous country.

title: Popular LGBTQ Influencer And Makeup Artist Mad Sandhu Shot Dead In Amritsar
content: Mad Sandhu was found lying on the road, blood-soaked, after suffering two gunshots; he had constantly faced homophobic trolling on social media, to which he would hit back by saying, "God has made me the way I am", and wouldn't hide his being gay.

title: Bhutan's 'Gateway To World' Takes Shape With Gelephu Airport Construction
content: The airfield package is one of the two largest remaining construction contracts for the airport, alongside the Passenger Terminal Building and associated landside works.

content: Romi has been granted bail in the Nabha jailbreak case by the Punjab and Haryana High Court, while a Nabha court has also granted him bail in a separate case registered under the Arms Act.

title: AAP Expels Punjab MLA For Alleging Lack Of Teachers In Government Schools
content: Aam Aadmi Party's Maur MLA Sukhbir Singh Maiserkhana has publicly raised concerns over teacher shortages in government schools -- an act AAP deemed an anti-party activity.

title: North Korea Tests AI-Enabled Ballistic Missile That Can 'Change Flight Orbit'
content: The launch took place days after Seoul's military demanded an apology from Pyongyang for a blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) that it blamed on the North.

title: 70-Year-Old Man Trapped Between Walls Of 2 Houses. Then, A Heroic Rescue
content: Vinod Vishnu Jadhav, a resident of Palghar, got stuck in a space between the walls that was less than one foot in width.

title: Congress Falls Back On A Fullback: Where Pargat Singh Fits In The Punjab Poll Play
content: Vijay Inder Singla, a Hindu face, was reportedly the frontrunner before the Congress replaced one Jat Sikh with another as its Punjab unit chief. How far does such arithmetic work in the state's politics? Pargat's appointment holds some of the answers.

title: 7 Arrested After Woman Stripped, Assaulted In Guwahati Bar
content: The arrests were made after police took note of viral social media videos purportedly showing the alleged assault, and registered a case on their own.

title: India Faces Sharp Rise In Power Shortage As September Demand Spikes
content: Actual power demand during April-August FY27 was 3.3 per cent higher than projected, suggesting that the country's electricity needs have been growing faster than expected.

title: Why Anthropic Is Asking Religious Leaders About AI Consciousness
content: The AI company has reportedly been consulting religious leaders and philosophers on morality, consciousness and how to make Claude "good". But Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman has warned that treating AI as if it has feelings could be dangerous.

title: 21 Gold, 27 Silver & 37 Bronze: India's medal frenzy at Asian Games ends with a bang
content: The Aichi-Nagoya campaign produced a mix of expected results and disappointments before India's strong finish changed the picture. As recently as Thursday, India were outside the top 10 in the medal table with only 10 gold medals.

title: Helicopters, influencers and nail art: The money trail of 2026 assembly elections
content: The BJP and Congress have filed their election expenditure reports following several assembly elections this year. The BJP recorded a hefty expenditure of Rs 529.39 crore across five states, whereas Congress spent Rs 248.55 crore. These contrasting figures unveil the distinct priorities of the political parties, particularly in West Bengal and Keralam.

title: What took 10 Google engineers six months now happens overnight, says Eric Schmidt
content: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says the best programmers no longer write code. Speaking at Harvard's John F. Kennedy Jr. Forum, Schmidt described an engineer who writes specifications and evaluation criteria, lets AI run overnight, and wakes up to finished work. He argued AI will make top engineers more valuable, automate core business operations like billing and logistics, and predicted artificial general intelligence (AGI) could arrive as early as 2029.

title: How landlord won tax relief on Rs 14.96 lakh demonetisation cash deposit
content: The Bangalore bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) recently held that rental income already disclosed to the income tax authorities can be considered as an identifiable source of cash deposited into a bank account at a later date. Even where a landlord claims to have collected rent in cash, the subsequent deposit of that money cannot be disregarded merely because the rental earnings have already been taxed.

title: Congress resets Team UP: 5 clear messages for BJP and Akhilesh Yadav
content: Congress has overhauled its Uttar Pradesh unit ahead of the 2027 UP assembly election, appointing three-time MLA Aradhana Misra Mona as state president and Imran Masood as working president. The Congress reshuffle brings Brahmin, Muslim, OBC, Dalit and women representation into its leadership team, signalling a push to rebuild its organisation, expand its social base and strengthen its position in talks with Samajwadi Party.

title: Russia to take 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year, Jaishankar tells panel
content: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar briefed a parliamentary committee on India's engagement with Russia and Ukraine. He highlighted bilateral trade expansion and India's aim to send skilled workers. The minister discussed India's diplomatic efforts to facilitate dialogue for ending the Ukraine conflict. Additionally, he noted the government's initiatives to release Indian nationals in the Russian military. Jaishankar emphasized India's commitment to secure economic interests and safeguard Indian citizens abroad.

title: Queensland farmer opened 4 campsites after drought; they brought in over A$50,000
content: Agritourism is gaining momentum among Australian farmers struggling with drought-related financial pressures. Landowners like Libby Rough are transforming their properties into camping havens, creating alternative income streams. This shift not only aids in sustaining their farms during tough times but also promotes local agricultural education among visitors. Moreover, local authorities are streamlining regulations to encourage this thriving sector, enhancing community engagement with farming practices.

title: Four Helene-damaged NC homes repaired after storm will now be demolished in FEMA buyouts
content: In the aftermath of Hurricane Helene, four homes in the Cottages at Cypress Run neighborhood in Hendersonville face demolition due to severe flooding. Previously, these homes were repaired through homeowner efforts and community volunteerism. To address the persistent flood threats, homeowners have chosen FEMA's voluntary buyouts, aligning with the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program's initiative to convert affected land into green spaces, thereby reducing future flood risks.

title: MacKenzie Scott gave $30M to housing nonprofit; a year later, it unveiled 10-year plan
content: MacKenzie Scott has made headlines with her unprecedented $30 million donation to Housing Trust Silicon Valley, marking the organization's largest-ever gift. This investment is set to bolster affordable housing options throughout the Bay Area, as the trust plans to enhance its loan fund and expand various housing initiatives over the next decade.

title: US released Asian lady beetles to fight pests; decades later, they became invasive
content: Originally imported to the United States for biological pest control, the multicoloured Asian lady beetle, or Harmonia axyridis, has turned invasive. Competing with native ladybugs, this species disrupts ecosystems. While it helps manage aphid populations, its autumn behavior drives adult beetles to invade homes, creating an unwanted nuisance. This case serves as a cautionary tale about the unintended effects of introducing nonnative species into local environments.

title: Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes' 1587 restaurant lawsuit takes new turn
content: Amid ongoing trademark issues, Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes are throwing their weight behind 1587 Prime, which has just garnered a spot on Yelp's list of Best New Restaurants for 2026. The dispute involves trademark claims from 1587 Sneakers, alleging infringement concerning their sneaker line. Seeking to distance the athletes from the legal matter, their lawyers are taking action while 1587 Prime thrives amid the conflict.

title: How Maria Sharapova built a $220 million fortune beyond tennis
content: Sharapova used her tennis success to build a bigger business career after retiring. Her estimated $220 million fortune has been tied to career earnings, global endorsements, Sugarpova and investments in consumer, wellness, fitness and technology companies, allowing the five-time Grand Slam champion to build a financial portfolio outside of professional tennis.

title: Akhilesh asks SP leaders to keep seat-sharing concerns with Congress internal
content: Akhilesh Yadav, president of the Samajwadi Party, encouraged leaders to express seat-sharing concerns privately. Tensions arose after Shiv Pal Singh Patel criticized Congress' demand for 150 seats in upcoming elections. Patel emphasized that Congress should receive a more realistic allocation based on their previous performance. Uttar Pradesh Congress president Aradhana Mishra stated that top leadership will decide the seat allocation.

title: Kolkata, AIFF pull out all stops for India vs Brazil but crowd stays away
content: In many ways, it was a historic occasion. Brazil hadn't faced a team as lower ranked than India in 28 years. India hadn't gone up against a team as higher ranked as Brazil since rankings were introduced in August 1993. It helps significantly that Kolkata raves over Brazil (and Argentina).

title: 'No deadline for Sheikh Hasina's return', says Indian high commissioner in Bangladesh
content: High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi addressed the extradition request for Sheikh Hasina from Bangladesh, stating that the matter is under legal review, preventing a set timeline for her repatriation. He clarified that India had no involvement in her arrival, citing the dire circumstances in Bangladesh. As relations between India and Bangladesh grow increasingly strained, the new Bangladeshi government remains resolute in pursuing Hasina's extradition.

title: Influencer Mad Sandhu shot dead in Amritsar
content: Mad Sandhu was shot dead on Saturday in the Pratap Nagar area of Amritsar, Punjab. Preliminary information suggests that assailants opened fire at him, resulting in his death. Police arrived at the scene shortly after receiving information about the shooting. An investigation has been launched to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident. The identities of the assailants remain unknown at this time.

title: Ukraine confirms India playing big role in mediating energy truce in Black Sea
content: Ukraine has expressed readiness to explore India's comprehensive proposal for ending the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict. During recent communications, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha emphasized the importance of India's mediation role. India's external affairs minister S Jaishankar affirmed continuous engagement with both Kyiv and Moscow regarding potential solutions. Ukraine is open to discussing limited ceasefire arrangements around energy infrastructure and safe Black Sea shipping.

title: We seem to be learning that currency depreciation is not always bad: Panagariya
content: Arvind Panagariya, chairman of the 16th Finance Commission, outlines the benefits of a weaker rupee for exports. He stresses that rising import costs can maintain the competitiveness of domestic products. The need for tariff cuts, elimination of quality control orders, and revision of bilateral investment treaties is emphasized. Panagariya also mentions the current economic stability and potential growth of 7-8%. He expresses optimism despite external challenges affecting growth prospects.

title: 'Parents oppose marriage': Andhra man kills 19-year-old girlfriend, jumps to death
content: Mahalakshmi, a young woman of 19, lost her life after a brutal knife attack by her ex-boyfriend, Chinna Rao, aged 22. The assault occurred at her home, where Chinna's persistent harassment, stemming from family opposition, culminated in violence. Mahalakshmi suffered grave injuries and passed away after four hours in the hospital. In a heartbreaking conclusion, Chinna leaped from a building, ending his life shortly after the attack.

title: 50 cities, 70,000 protesters: Spain’s housing crisis fuels nationwide anger
content: Protests erupted in multiple Spanish cities, including Madrid, following the rejection of rental protection measures by parliament. Tens of thousands of demonstrators demanded action on the housing crisis affecting vulnerable renters. The anger was sparked by the eviction of an elderly woman, who became a symbol of the housing struggles. The rising rental costs have made affordable housing increasingly out of reach for many citizens.

title: 'Drishyam 3' BO day 2: Ajay Devgn starrer set to enter Rs 100 cr club today
content: 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion', starring Ajay Devgn, has made waves at the box office, garnering an impressive Rs 62 crore on debut and an additional Rs 25.50 crore the following day. With total earnings in India surpassing Rs 104.49 crore, projections suggest continued success. Directed by Abhishek Pathak, this film successfully navigates cast changes while captivating audiences since its premiere on October 2, 2026.

title: Asian Games 2026 Medal Tally: Golden run in hockey, cricket takes India into top 4
content: India moved up to fourth place in the Asian Games 2026 medal tally after a big medal-winning day on Saturday. India added five gold medals across wrestling, golf, hockey, cricket and archery to take their overall tally to 85 medals - 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze.

title: 'Attacked with hammer': RSS functionary Rameshwar Tiwari dies after assault in UP
content: Rameshwar Tiwari was killed following an assault during a clash in Bheekam Chhapra village. His wife, Amrita Devi, filed an FIR against several named and unnamed individuals involved in the incident. Four police personnel have been suspended due to negligence in handling the situation prior to the attack. The conflict reportedly stemmed from an old land property issue between families in the area.

title: India explode in 2nd half, crush Malaysia 5-1 to retain Asian Games gold; seal LA28 spot
content: India had never won successive Asian Games gold medals, making Saturday's final an opportunity to create history. Harmanpreet Singh-led India made the most of it as they successfully defended their title.

title: India's golden Saturday: Hockey, cricket, wrestling, golf and archery deliver golds
content: India produced one of their biggest medal hauls of the Asian Games on Saturday, with gold medals coming in men's hockey, T20 cricket, wrestling, golf and archery. The men's hockey team capped the day by beating Malaysia 5-1 in the final to retain their Asian Games title and book a place at the 2028 Olympics. India's medal tally now stands at 85 medals - 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze.

title: Major lapse by Israeli intel? Over 12 Omani pilots flew to Tel Aviv despite ban
content: Israeli passengers, the captain and other pilots on board intervened, allowing the plane to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Most of the passengers were Israeli and were later flown from Saudi Arabia to Israel. Oman does not have diplomatic relations with Israel. According to the report, rules introduced after 2020 Abraham Accords prohibit pilots from countries that do not have relations with Israel from flying into the country.

title: 'Dragged to basement, assaulted': 7 held after woman partially stripped at nightclub
content: Seven individuals, including a nightclub manager, were arrested following an incident of assault at The Locals nightclub. The incident occurred after a drunken altercation where a woman was reportedly assaulted by bouncers. Police conducted an investigation after receiving information about the assault and reviewed CCTV footage from the nightclub. A video circulating on social media showed the woman being assaulted, leading to police action.
